official_finding.summary: The motor vehicle carrier Golden Ray capsized in St Simons Sound on 8 September 2019 shortly after departing the Port of Brunswick; the NTSB (MAR-21/01) attributed the capsizing to the chief officer's incorrect ballast entries, which left the ship with inadequate stability. During the 2020-2021 wreck-removal operation, oil repeatedly escaped the wreck; the largest release began 31 July 2021 when a vent pipe was exposed during the partial lift of Section Six, and tidal flows carried oil out of the environmental protection barrier onto St Simons Island and Jekyll Island shorelines and marsh. The source is the wreck itself; the salvage vessels operating on scene are pollution responders, not the polluter.

responsible_parties.name: M/V Golden Ray (wreck)
responsible_parties.role: fixed source of the discharge; owner/operator Hyundai Glovis, the designated responsible party for cleanup

responsible_parties.name: T&T Salvage / VB-10000
responsible_parties.role: salvage contractor on scene — a responder, to be EXCLUDED from suspects

official_finding.source_name: USCG / Georgia DNR — St Simons Sound Incident Response Unified Command releases (July-Aug 2021); NTSB Marine Accident Report MAR-21/01 (capsizing cause)
official_finding.volume_reported: unquantified during the 31 Jul 2021 release (Unified Command: 'unknown quantity'); shoreline oiling documented on St Simons and Jekyll Islands
official_finding.caveat: There is no SAR-visible slick in any Sentinel-1 pass over the enclosed, sheltered sound. This is a known-source case: the origin is the fixed wreck at ~31.13 N, 81.40 W. The salvage fleet must appear as exclusions, not suspects.
